mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates monetary easing, which lowers discount rates and increases equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1 percentage points over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% within the prior month signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE rises above 5.0% within the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% and employment (PAYEMS) by more than 0.2% over the prior 3 months indicates economic contraction, reducing corporate earnings and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decline > 0.5% and PAYEMS decline > 0.2% over prior 3 months
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where both INDPRO and PAYEMS decline by at least 0.5% and 0.2% respectively over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a CPIAUCSL rise above 2.0% annualized signals inflationary pressures that may trigger a Federal Reserve rate hike, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises above 2.0% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand and economic growth, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where HOUST increases by at least 0.5% over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 within the prior month signals manufacturing weakness, reducing economic activity and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO falls below 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.1% and inflation (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.2% over the prior 3 months indicates monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rise > 0.1% and CPIAUCSL rise > 0.2% over prior 3 months
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise by at least 0.1% and 0.2% respectively over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market slack regime, a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.8% within the prior month signals an economic slowdown, reducing corporate demand and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the labor market slack regime, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises above 4.8%.
